title: AI-300: Optimizing Generative AI Systems and Model Performance

objectives.text: Optimize retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) performance and accuracy

children.text: Optimize retrieval performance by tuning similarity thresholds, chunk sizes, and retrieval strategies
Select and fine-tune embedding models for domain-specific use cases and accuracy improvements
Implement and optimize hybrid search approaches combining semantic and keyword-based retrieval
Evaluate and improve RAG system performance by using relevance metrics and A/B testing frameworks

objectives.text: Implement advanced fine-tuning and model customization

children.text: Design and implement advanced fine-tuning methods
Create and manage synthetic data for fine-tuning
Monitor and optimize fine-tuned model performance
Manage a fine-tuned model from development through production deployment

demos.title: Demo: Tune chunks and similarity cutoffs in Azure AI Search

steps.title: Query one Azure AI Search Free-tier index with a chunk_size pre-filter to select 64-, 128-, or 192-token chunks of the same corpus, encoded with all-MiniLM-L6-v2.
Vary vector candidate depth and apply a cosine cutoff in the Python client after converting a pure single-vector search score; inspect retained and rejected results.
Compare Recall@k, boundary failures, and latency while changing one control at a time; retain the configuration that supplies useful evidence.

expected_evidence: Chunk-size-controlled Azure search responses
Retained and rejected single-vector candidates with converted cosine values
Recall@k, boundary-failure and latency comparison

demos.title: Demo: Run hybrid search and semantic reranking in Azure

steps.title: Send text and vector queries together to Azure AI Search; compare its reciprocal rank fusion results with separate keyword and vector searches.
Vary vector weight and candidate depth, then enable semantic reranking with 50 vector candidates and inspect search and reranker scores separately.
Compare exact identifiers and paraphrased questions on the same validation set; keep relevance gains without hiding query-type regressions.

expected_evidence: Keyword, vector and reciprocal-rank-fused result comparisons
Vector-weight, candidate-depth and semantic reranker response fields
Exact-identifier and paraphrase validation results

demos.title: Demo: Evaluate RAG variants with Azure services

steps.title: Run the Python experiment runner against two configurations of the same Azure AI Search index and the same gpt-5.6-luna deployment in Microsoft Foundry, holding the prompt and generation settings fixed.
Compare Recall@k, nDCG@k, manually reviewed answer support, and latency using real retrieval and generated responses; inspect a response against its source and check for regressions.
Assign synthetic sessions consistently to A or B, retain exposure and outcome logs in Azure ML with MLflow, and analyze the declared primary metric and stop rule.

expected_evidence: Assignments to fixed retrieval variants and matching Foundry generation settings
Recall@k, nDCG@k, manually reviewed answer support, latency, source checks and regression checks
MLflow exposure/outcome logs, primary metric and stop-rule analysis

demos.title: Demo: Fine-tune domain embeddings in Azure ML

steps.title: Configure a Sentence Transformers contrastive training script with reviewed positive pairs and hard negatives, then submit an Azure ML CPU command job.
Inspect a completed job with matching code, environment, and data versions; select its checkpoint from validation metrics and retain the job output.
Encode corpus and queries with the selected checkpoint; populate its dedicated vector field in the same index, filter to the same chunk_size, and compare held-out relevance with the baseline fields.

demos.title: Demo: Monitor Azure traffic and verify rollback

steps.title: Configure an Azure Monitor alert on Request Latency P95; inspect latency by deployment, Requests Per Minute by deployment and status-code class, and each deployment’s CPU and memory utilization.
Allocate 90 percent of managed endpoint traffic to the baseline and 10 percent to the candidate; send labeled test traffic and retain deployment identities in the evidence.

Inspect a real candidate gate failure from a predeclared, controlled rollback test and stop promotion; keep the baseline’s normal gate unchanged and distinguish the exercise from production-user outcomes.
Restore 100 percent traffic to the baseline, then verify the routed model identity, responses, and recovered operational behavior.

expected_evidence: Latency, request/status-class, CPU/memory metrics and Request Latency P95 alert
90/10 traffic configuration and labeled test responses with deployment identities
Real predeclared controlled candidate gate failure, unchanged normal baseline gate and stopped promotion
100/0 restored traffic with routed identity, response and recovery checks
